title: Weather Station Layout
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: E-Paper Display
Weather Station
Update Schedule
Battery Life
Layout Design
description: Interactive p5.js design tool for a 152 x 152 e-paper weather display. Students drag and resize the time, indoor and forecast panels, choose update intervals, and simulate a day to count refreshes and WiFi connections and estimate battery life on 500 mAh.

educational.topic: Designing a weather station display and its update schedule
learningObjectives: Design a readable layout for a small e-paper weather display
Evaluate how each panel's update interval changes refreshes, WiFi connections and battery life
Justify an update schedule by matching it to how fast each kind of data changes

keyQuestions: Which kind of data needs to update most often, and which least?
Why is a WiFi fetch more expensive than a display refresh?
How big must the time digits be to read from across a room?
commonMisconceptions: Every panel should update as often as possible to stay accurate
A bigger display area is free on e-paper (larger partial refreshes take longer)
assessmentOpportunities: Compare battery life for several schedules
Defend a final layout and schedule in writing

controls.label: Drag and resize panels
controls.description: Move a panel by dragging it; resize it by dragging its corner.

controls.label: Simulate day / Pause / Continue
controls.description: Runs a 24-hour timeline. Opens paused; nothing runs until it is pressed.

controls.label: Reset layout
controls.description: Restores the starting layout and clears results.
